title: Triggered perturbation and cohort contracts for Optimize evals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define acceptance contracts, perturbation test matrix, and cohort-triggered rollback conditions for Optimize evals so model/quantization changes can be safely rolled out without unexpected regressions in key product cohorts.
background: We have a growing surface of Optimize evals (prompt sets, A/B tests, multi-metric signals) but current gates are brittle for asymmetric regressions and long-tail prompt perturbations. Recent internal incidents showed small distributional shifts and prompt formatting changes causing subtle quality drops for specific cohorts (e.g., legal templates, short chatbot intents). The goal is a pragmatic, measurable contract that combines targeted perturbation tests, cohort bucketing, and a staged canary/rollback choreography.
proposal: Introduce a triggered perturbation harness and cohort contracts that run automatically as part of canary and pre-rollout validation. Key ideas: (1) perturbation matrix that applies small, realistic transformations to prompt inputs (token-level noise, punctuation changes, instruction paraphrases, entity obfuscation), (2) map customer cohorts to risk tiers and tailored sentinel prompt subsets, (3) compute a composite regression score combining fidelity, hallucination rate, and safety signals with variance-aware thresholds, (4) define multi-window detection (1h, 6h, 24h) and escalation rules that either throttle canary traffic, pause rollout, or automatically rollback based on severity and persistence.
acceptance_criteria: Perturbation harness implemented and attached to existing Optimize eval runner with documented perturbation matrix (at least 8 perturbation modes) and reproducible seeds
Cohort mapping defined for top 6 customer cohorts by traffic; each cohort has a sentinel set of 200 prompts sampled from production + 50 synthetic perturbations
Composite regression score computed per-cohort and per-model using weighted metrics (fidelity 50%, hallucination 30%, safety/regression flags 20%) and exposed via Console metrics

Alerting thresholds: first-level warning at composite drop >= 3% vs baseline for a single 1-hour window; actionable pause condition at drop >= 6% sustained over three non-overlapping 1-hour windows within a 6-hour period

A/B rollback criteria defined: in an A/B test, if cohort-level composite delta >= 4% and overall customer-visible negative delta >= 2% for 4 consecutive evaluation windows, traffic is automatically reverted to control
Grace windows: small, transient spikes (<2% composite drift, isolated to single window) create alerts but do not auto-pause; they are annotated in runbook and retained for 14 days
Playbook entries created and linked in Console: (a) throttling to 10% canary traffic, (b) pause and notify SRE/PM, (c) immediate rollback with postmortem ticket template
Dashboard widgets added to per-route Optimize pages showing cohort composite score, per-metric breakdown, and perturbation failure examples (top 10 failed prompts)
E2E test that simulates a regression (synthetic drop of 7% composite on a sentinel cohort) reliably triggers the auto-pause and rollback paths in sandbox environment
success_metrics: Reduction in undetected cohort regressions post-deploy by at least 60% compared to baseline quarter
Average time-to-detect for cohort regressions reduced from 3.2 hours to <= 1.5 hours
False-positive auto-pause rate kept below 1% of canaries per quarter
Number of rollbacks caused by asymmetrical cohort regressions reduced by 50%
rollout_plan: 1) Implement harness in sandbox and run nightly perturbation suites on candidate models (sprint 1). 2) Expose cohort composite metrics in Console (sprint 2). 3) Run staged canaries with auto-throttle (10% -> 25% -> 50%) under observation (sprint 3). 4) Promote auto-pause/rollback to production guardrail for Dedicated and Hosted after one-week shadow runs and stakeholder sign-off.
tasks: Define perturbation matrix and generate canonical examples (PM + Research)
Extend Optimize eval runner to accept perturbation transforms and seed controls (ENG)
Build cohort selector + sentinel sampler using production traffic buckets (ENG/Analytics)
Implement composite scoring and per-cohort baselining logic (ENG)
Console: dashboard panels + alert hooks + per-prompt failure examples (DX/Frontend)
SRE: implement auto-throttle, pause, and rollback API hooks and test in sandbox
Write playbook and runbook with step-by-step escalation paths and postmortem template (PM + SRE)
Create integration tests that inject known degradation and assert correct automation behavior (ENG)
Coordinate beta with 3 pilot customers and collect feedback (PM/Customer Success)
notes: Avoid overfitting thresholds to a single heavy-traffic customer; use weighted baselines and robust statistics (median + MAD)
Perturbation types should be realistic — prioritize transformations seen in production parse failures
We will version perturbation suites so we can reproduce past evaluations for audits
Consider golden prompt anchors for high-risk cohorts (legal, medical) with stricter thresholds and mandatory human review
